rationale: Neither candidate recovers the ground truth's actual concerns (benchmark-harness dedup debate, missing profiling/VRAM/baseline evidence, HTTP-vs-WebSocket speed-control asymmetry, duration_factor bounds duplication across talker/decoder) — X even inspected the exact s2mel_decoder duration_factor code the ground truth flagged and concluded 'no issue found,' actively missing it. X compensates with tightly evidence-cited, low-risk findings (test-marker deselection, version-string mismatches, i18n TN gaps) that are easy to verify but mostly process/doc-level. Y surfaces deeper functional-correctness bugs (uninitialized mel_head.bias, silent zero-audio fallback, 2.0 regression risk, renderer-selection scope creep) that are more speculative and harder to verify blind, but closer in spirit to the ground truth's blocking-severity validation concerns, and its review is better structured with concrete code-level fixes. Given comparably poor recall for both, Y edges out on the depth/usefulness of its findings and actionability.
